name: expanding-menu
summary: A nav bar whose panel drops in behind a two-layer cover that unrolls from the top while the content behind it splits and parallaxes, reversing on close.

duration.description: Seconds the open takes. Upstream's timeline defaults.duration.

coverDuration.description: Seconds the cover wrap takes to settle from 1.1 to 1. Upstream's cover.wrap duration.

parallax.description: Percent the content behind the cover splits by. Upstream's content img / title offsets.

deviations.what: The cover and the three content panels paint the --fx-image and --fx-cover-image custom properties instead of the demo's inline background-image URLs.
deviations.why: Codrops ships the demo's photographs under separate terms and this library redistributes none of them. The defaults are layered gradients, so the two-layer cover still reads as a picture sliding through its own window, and a site author points the properties at real pictures with one declaration.

deviations.what: Durations and label offsets are milliseconds: every upstream second value is multiplied by the SEC constant, 1000, and GSAP's 'menu+=0.6' label arithmetic is written out as MENU + 0.6 * SEC.
deviations.why: GSAP counts in seconds and anime.js in milliseconds, and anime positions a timeline child by time rather than by a label expression. Keeping upstream's own numbers and doing the arithmetic in one place is what makes the schedule readable against the source.

deviations.what: GSAP's power4.inOut and power3.inOut easings are written as anime's inOutQuint and inOutQuart, and power4 as outQuint.
deviations.why: GSAP names its power curves by exponent minus one and defaults a bare name to .out; anime names them after the polynomial and spells the direction. Same curves.

deviations.what: The isAnimating latch is dropped: a click during the open or the close reverses the timeline from where it is rather than being ignored.
deviations.why: Upstream's latch exists because its timeline is played and reversed from a paused state and a second call mid-flight would fight the first. anime's play() and reverse() seek from the current playhead, so the flip is continuous, and a control that ignores a click for 1.2 seconds reads as broken.

deviations.what: Under prefers-reduced-motion the menu still opens and closes; the timeline is seeked to its end or its start instead of being played.
deviations.why: Effect contract: mount() stays at rest and must never trap content behind an animation. This panel is navigation, so hiding it from a visitor who asked for stillness would take the links away rather than take the motion away. Seeking gives the same end state with no travel.

deviations.what: Every element is resolved inside the mounted section rather than from the document, class names are ours, and the timeline is reverted and both listeners removed on destroy.
deviations.why: Upstream queries the document at module scope and never tears the effect down. An effect is one section among several and a page may carry this one twice, so two mounts would otherwise drive each other's cover; and a destroy mid-open would leave the section frozen under a half-unrolled panel.
